About the two index lines. Health is resting heart rate and overnight heart-rate variability; activity is step count and active calories. Each input is scored against my own median and spread, so 50 is a typical week of mine and 10 points is one standard deviation — the number says “a better week than most weeks here”, not “a heart rate of 39”. It is not a clinical score and it does not compare to anyone else’s. The faint line is the week; the solid one is an eight-week trailing mean, which is the only resolution at which either of these says anything — week to week they are one bad night and one long Saturday.

The two rings on the health line are its lowest and highest sustained stretches — placed on the eight-week mean, not on single weeks, because a milestone should mark a period rather than a blip. The worst single week on record scores 16; the trend around it reads 32, and 32 is the honest number for how that stretch actually went. One caveat travels with the low: it falls inside the dashed stretch, so it is a resting-heart-rate reading being compared against later ones that also had HRV behind them.

Two things the lines cannot do. Where the line is dashed it is running on fewer inputs than the rest of itself: nothing recorded HRV before April 2023, so the health line over that stretch is resting heart rate alone, and it is a weaker claim wearing the same colour. And activity here means movement, not training — it counts a long day on my feet much like a hard session, and lifting barely registers. A flat activity line through a heavy block is a limit of the instrument, not a rest week.

The phases

Two tiers, and they are not interchangeable. A–E come from the daily fasted-morning series, which only exists from July 2025; their evidence column is the share of days with a reading — a rate over 13% coverage is not the same kind of number as a rate over 91%. N1–N3 come from monthly notebook readings taken at no fixed time of day, so they are not fasted-AM and their rates cannot be compared to A–E's — their evidence column is a raw reading count. Where neither can support a rate, none is given. Click any row to isolate that phase on the chart.
